newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may join Zaire intervention force.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may join Zaire intervention force.

text.p: Brazil may join any United Nations intervention force sent to eastern Zaire, the Foreign Ministry said on Thursday.

The ministry said in a statement that Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien, whose country will take the lead in the operation, had asked Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to contribute to the force.
"The president of the Republic reacted favourably to the request for a Brazilian contribution, which we are now in the process of defining," the ministry said.
General Alberto Cardoso, head of the Military House in the Presidency, said in a briefing with foreign journalists late on Wednesday that "Brazil will probably be able to help" in Zaire.

Noting Brazilian peacekeeping experience under U.N. auspices in Mozambique and Angola, Cardoso said Brasilia envisaged more active participation in international peace operations following the introduction last week of a new National Policy of Defence.
"One of the objectives of the (new) policy is the projection of the country abroad," said the general, who is not related to the president.
He added: "(In Zaire), genocide is taking place. President Cardoso is very shocked by what is happening."
